In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the influence of water vapor transport is not negligible and should be considered in the modeling of water vapor sorption experiments on samples with a small mass.
the water vapor sorption behavior of small wood specimens is a complex phenomenon that can not be reduced to a simplified model.
water vapour sorptions experiments with small sample sizes are influenced by water vapour transport processes and thus should be considered in the interpretation of the results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sorption kinetics is a function of both water vapour transport and water vapour sorbtion within the sample.
water vapour sorptions on small samples should be performed with a high humidity step size and that the sample thickness should be as large as possible.
the sorption kinetics for small sample sizes can be described by a diffusion equation including the sink/source term and a correction factor for the influence of stagnant air.
The main takeaway from our work is that
water vapour transport is not only a phenomenon of the cell wall, but also of the air above the sample surface.
sorption kinetics of wood and other hygroscopic material can only be accurately described if the influence of water transport is considered.
sorption experiments on grained samples are only comparable if the sample thickness is identical.
